title: Hybrid IO Floors with Gracebanding for Burst Streams - Pilot Design
creator: Maya Ortiz
description: Problem: Customers with bursty streaming use cases (long-lived websocket/HTTP2 streams) are exposed to unpredictable bills under a pure per-token model and small-volume customers see disproportionate unit costs due to minimums that don't account for directionality. Goal: design an experiment that decouples ingress/output pricing, introduces a short-term "graceband" credit for streaming bursts, and pilots blended floor logic that improves unit economics for steady output-heavy workloads while protecting revenue for low-volume noisy customers.
hypothesis: If we apply a hybrid IO floor that attributes a small portion of minimums to ingress vs egress and credit short bursts via a graceband, then (a) average effective price for steady output-heavy customers will fall by >=12%, (b) billed revenue leakage will remain <3% relative to control, and (c) we will see a net NRR improvement for mid-market customers using streaming features.
success_criteria: Primary: increase in paid utilization (paid tokens / API tokens) for target cohort by >=8% within 30d. Revenue guardrails: overall billed revenue delta vs control within +/-3%. Secondary: decreased churn signal on trial-to-paid for customers with streaming use cases.
experiment_design: A/B test spanning 30 days with random assignment at account level. Treatment implements: 1) separate per-token rates for input/output (configurable): sample starting point input=$0.00028/token, output=$0.00125/token; 2) blended minimum floor applied per billing window with direction attribution: e.g., a $5 minimum is credited as 40% ingress / 60% egress for billing attribution and reporting; 3) streaming graceband: first 60 seconds of a stream (or first 512 tokens) are eligible for a transient credit up to $0.15 per stream to absorb handshake/chatty clients; 4) rolling monthly reconciliation: if grace credits exceed thresholds, flag account for follow-up. Control remains current unified-per-token + global minimum behavior.
segments: Target: mid-market and developer-tier customers with at least one active streaming route in last 14 days and median output/input token ratio >= 2. Exclusions: enterprise committed accounts (we will coordinate contract addenda separately).
sample_size_and_power: We estimate needing ~1,200 accounts per arm to detect an 8% change in effective unit price with 80% power assuming baseline stdev from prior experiments. We'll run for 30 days (expected ~60k invoiced events).
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag gated rollout in billing service; 2) Internal QA on staging with synthetic streams; 3) Open to 10% of eligible accounts for first 48 hours; 4) Ramp to 100% of treatment cohort over 3 days if no anomalies; 5) Daily revenue and SLO check-ins; 6) Freeze and rollback criteria defined (see risks).
implementation_tasks: billing: add ingress/egress attribution logic and blended floor computation (PR # TBD)
metering: emit ingress_tokens and egress_tokens per request and per-stream markers
console: add per-route breakdown for floor attribution and grace credits
billing-tests: end-to-end invoice simulation harness for 30-day windows
docs: update pricing FAQ and public API docs to reflect IO split and graceband behavior
legal: draft contract addendum language for enterprise opt-in/out
risks: Upfront revenue dip if graceband credits are larger than modeled
Complexity in invoices leading to increased support tickets
Edge cases where streaming connectors reopen streams rapidly and exhaust credits
Enterprise customers require contract-level exceptions which complicate rollout
mitigations: Set conservative graceband size for initial pilot, implement throttled graceband per account, add invoice line-item explanation and sample invoices to public docs, and coordinate an enterprise addendum template with Legal and AMs to handle opt-outs.
contract_considerations: For enterprise customers we will offer: (a) explicit addendum that opts into the hybrid-floor logic; (b) ability to set a fixed monthly minimum in $ with IO attribution reporting; (c) audit clause to reconcile heavy graceband usage across the term; (d) standard SLOs unchanged. Legal to prepare template text and a short Q&A for RMs.
support_and_ops: On-call playbook for billing anomalies, dashboard showing delta vs expected invoiced revenue, automated alert if grace credits exceed 2% of monthly ARR in pilot cohort, triage runbook for escalations to Billing Eng.
data_and_reporting: Daily aggregated report: cohort-level effective unit prices, graceband credit usage, invoice delta vs modeled, per-account flags. Post-30d analysis will include propensity-adjusted revenue lift and customer-level qualitative sampling (interviews with 10 affected customers).
decision_criteria: If experiment meets primary success criteria and billed revenue delta is within +/-3%, proceed to wider rollout with parameter tuning. If revenue shortfall >3% or support contacts increase >25% vs control, halt and iterate.
